_about: Parameters of sim/water.py (surface water + combined sewer). Every value has a source; 'calibrated' = tuned on the 31.12.2022 replay vs the SFPUC 100-yr map and 311 reports (see runs/dev_water/). Loaded by sim.water.default_params().

alpha.source: Bates, Horritt & Fewtrell 2010, J. Hydrol. 387:33-45, eq. 14: CFL coefficient 0.2-0.7 for the local-inertial scheme

theta.source: de Almeida, Bates, Freer & Souvignet 2012, Water Resour. Res. 48 W05528: theta 0.7-0.9 suppresses oscillations

hmin.source: LISFLOOD-FP user manual v8 (Univ. Bristol): depth threshold 1e-3 m for wet/dry faces

fr_max.source: Froude limiter as in LISFLOOD-FP / de Almeida & Bates 2013 (WRR 49): caps spurious supercritical fluxes; 3 allows real supercritical flow on SF's 10-30 % grades

dt_max.source: numerical choice (upper bound on the adaptive step, keeps rain/inlet coupling explicit-stable)

flood_thr.source: FEMA / Hazus: water above ~10 cm on streets impedes traffic and starts entering doorways; used for flood_duration_s

edge_freeboard_m.source: model boundary choice: tile-edge free outflow only where ground is > 0.5 m above the storm's peak tide (low edge cells continue as Bay/shore outside the tile)

intertidal_z.source: NOAA CO-OPS 9414290 datums: MLLW ~0.0 m NAVD88, MHHW 1.798 m; open cells below MLLW+0.5 touching the Bay are water (hydro-flattened lidar)

i_design_mm_h.source: calibrated equivalent conveyance intensity; SFPUC Sewer System Improvement Program level of service = 5-year 3-hour design storm (SFPUC SSIP Levels of Service, 2016); NOAA Atlas 14 at 37.7765N 122.405W: 5-yr 60-min depth 18 mm, 10-yr 21 mm (data/reference/storm/noaa_atlas14_pfds_sf_37.7765_-122.405_mm.csv)

c_imp.source: Rational method runoff coefficient, paved/roof 0.7-0.95: ASCE/WEF MOP 77 Design and Construction of Urban Stormwater Management Systems (1992) Table 5.4

c_perv.source: Rational method, lawns/parks 0.1-0.35: ASCE/WEF MOP 77 (1992) Table 5.4

store_mm.source: calibrated on the 31.12.2022 replay: in-pipe + transport/storage-box volume as an equivalent depth over the sub-basin (SFPUC combined system with transport/storage boxes, SFPUC Sewer System Master Plan 2010; citywide volume not verified here)

pipe_depth_m.source: typical combined-sewer cover + diameter below grate in SF (SFPUC Subdivision Regulations / standard catch-basin details, 1.5-3 m)

a_manhole_m2.source: catch-basin / manhole shaft plan area ~0.6-1.2 m2 (SF DPW standard plans); free surface area once the sewer is surcharged

v0_frac.source: dry-weather flow occupies ~15 % of combined-sewer capacity: SFPUC ~80 Mgal/d dry vs ~500 Mgal/d wet-weather (sfpuc.gov 'Our Sewer System')

basin_km2.source: model discretisation: SF's 8 urban watersheds are subdivided into ~0.5-1 km2 sub-sewersheds in the SFPUC Sewer System Master Plan hydraulic model

cw.source: FHWA HEC-22 Urban Drainage Design Manual 3rd ed. (2009) eq. 4-26: grate in sag weir coefficient 1.66 (SI)

perim_m.source: perimeter of a ~0.6 x 0.9 m SF catch-basin grate (curb side excluded): HEC-22 sag-inlet weir length

a_open_m2.source: clear opening of a ~0.6 x 0.9 m grate (~55 % open), HEC-22 chart 9/10

inlet_mult.source: inlet capacity per data/grid/inlets.json (FHWA HEC-22 interception, sim/prep.py)

clog_max.source: FHWA HEC-22 (2009) inlets in sag: design practice assumes ~50 % grate clogging; SFPUC Adopt-a-Drain: leaves clog drains in storms

clog_tree_radius_m.source: model assumption: street trees within ~15 m (about 2 tree spacings) shed leaves into an inlet

clog_trees_full.source: model assumption: 3+ nearby street trees give the full HEC-22 50 % clogging; fewer scale linearly; drain clearing (plan) restores 1.0

psi_m.source: Green-Ampt wetting-front suction, sandy loam 110 mm: Rawls, Brakensiek & Miller 1983, J. Hydraul. Eng. 109(1) Table 1

porosity.source: effective porosity sandy loam/loam 0.41-0.43: Rawls et al. 1983 Table 1

root_m.source: street-tree root plate depth ~0.4-1 m (most roots in the top 0.6 m): Dupuy, Fourcaud & Stokes 2007 review of root anchorage, Plant Soil

pit_root_m.source: street tree basin soil depth ~3 ft (SF Better Streets Plan tree basin guidance; model assumption)

pit_frac.source: tree basin ~3x3 to 4x4 ft (~1-1.5 m2) of a 16 m2 cell (SF Better Streets Plan street tree guidance)

pit_ksat_mm_h.source: sandy loam Ks ~11-30 mm/h (Rawls et al. 1983) reduced for urban compaction (Pitt, Chen, Clark, Swenson & Ong 2008, J. Irrig. Drain. Eng. 134(5))

sf_land_km2.source: US Census Bureau 2020 Gazetteer: San Francisco city land area 46.9 mi2

dry_mgd.source: SFPUC 'Our Sewer System' (sfpuc.gov): combined system treats ~80 Mgal/day in dry weather

wet_mgd.source: SFPUC: up to ~500 Mgal/day treated citywide in wet weather (sfpuc.gov sewer system overview)

court_max_m2.source: model assumption: SF block interiors / rear-yard open space enclosed by buildings (25x100 ft lots, mid-block open space up to ~0.5 ha) drain via private area drains to the building sewer lateral (SF Plumbing Code: yard drains connect to the building sewer)

ext_upstream_m.source: calibrated: length of upstream sewershed beyond tile edges where ground falls into the tile (Mission Creek / Channel watershed drains from Twin Peaks & Bernal Heights, ~2-3 km to the divide; SFPUC Urban Watershed Assessment)

c_ext.source: Rational method, residential multi-unit 0.6-0.75: ASCE/WEF MOP 77 (1992) Table 5.4
